To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the quantum field theory of moving mirrors, in the functional Schrodinger-picture, is equivalent to the quantum mechanics of charged particle in an electromagnetic field.

we have shown how to construct the functional analogue of a quantum mechanical charged particle in an arbitrary external magnetic field, and how to use the result to solve the problem of moving mirrors upon which quantum field satisfy Dirichlet conditions.

the functional quantum field theory of moving mirrors is the analogue of the quantum-mechanical motion of a charged particle with a magnetic moment in an external magnetic flux, and that the analogue of the Aharonov-Bohm effect in this context is the analogue of gravitational-collapse.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the quantum theory of a system of a single scalar field interacting with a pair of mirrors, one of which moves in a prescribed manner and the other is stationary.
the formulation of the problem of accelerating boundaries for quantum fields, with the associated effect of the Hawking radiation, in terms of the functional Schrödiner picture.
the problem of quantum fields in a functional Schrödigner representation, with the associated problem of the Hawking effect in the context of gravitational collapse.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the Schrodinger picture, the problem of arbitrarily moving Dirichlet mirrors is solved in terms of a non-separable mode expansion.
the Hawking radiation is a consequence of the non-separablility of the mode expansion, and that the latter is in turn a consequence of the existence of a functional field-strength.
the functional Schrodinger formulation of accelerating mirrors provides a natural setting for the description of Hawking radiation in a quantum field theory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the functional analogue of a magnetic field is a non-vanishing second-rank antisymmetrical functional of the mirror motion, which in the present case is a functional of the mirror velocity, and that this is the source of non-separability in the mode expansion.
the quantum field theory of a system of mirrors and quantum field in Schrodinger picture can be solved exactly for arbitrary moving mirrors.
we have found a way to formulate the problem of moving mirrors in the functional Schrodinger-picture, and have solved it for a special case of interest.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the functional Schrodinger formulation is the appropriate framework for the analysis of quantum field theory in curved space-time, and the functional analogue of a magnetic field is the key to the non-separabilities in the theory.
the quantum field on the mirrors is in a non-separable state, even if the mirrors are initially in the vacuum state.
, in the presence of moving boundaries, the quantum fields are not separable into a product of spatial and time-dependences.
